text:
The news in Chicago this week isn't a result, it's a shoulder. Connor Bedard is out, and Jeff Blashill said the Blackhawks are gathering information to choose between rehab and surgery, with Bedard gone at least through the coming road trip, per Scott Powers. Mark Lazerus wrote that the team always knew there was a risk of the right shoulder "coming back out" after last year's injury. Bedard had 18 points in 15 games. Whatever the decision, the season around him now has a different shape.

Frank Nazar is the man in the spotlight in the meantime. He has 8 points in his last 10 and goals in three straight, and he's next in line for Bedard's minutes by how Blashill has used his forwards. The Blackhawks also beat Toronto 6-3 on Tuesday, though Spencer Knight was asked afterward about blowing a 4-0 lead along the way. Bowen Byram (upper body) skated in a non-contact jersey this morning. Chicago remains a team our numbers are hard on: 42% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five, a -33 goal difference, under 1% to make the playoffs. Knight is at -2.2 saves above expected; Arvid Söderblom cleared waivers to Rockford.

Columbus has its own trouble. The Blue Jackets are winless in five, outscored 21-8, and the chances say that is only partly bad luck (46% of the expected goals). Jet Greaves has lost six straight starts, which is why Cam Talbot is back in: he's at +5.2 saves above expected this season and +3.7 over his last five starts. Sean Monahan is out, Dmitri Voronkov has taken his spot beside Valeri Nichushkin, and Zach Werenski keeps turning up in trade-request speculation that nobody involved has confirmed.

Our numbers lean Columbus, 3.24 expected goals to 2.77, partly because Chicago gives up the third-most expected goals per 60. Our sleepers are both Blue Jackets: Mathieu Olivier (22% to score, one goal from 50 for his career) and Kent Johnson, whose minutes are up, at 61% for a point.
headline: Chicago waits on Bedard's shoulder; Columbus waits on a win
